newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT- Counties coach laments prop's suspension.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT- Counties coach laments prop's suspension.

text.p: AUCKLAND, Sept 17 - Counties-Manukau rugby coach Mac McCallion is "flabbergasted" that his prop Lee Lidgard's suspension for illegal rucking of an Otago player nine days ago wasn't overturned, NZPA reports.
The appeal by Counties of the two-week suspension was dismissed by the New Zealand Rugby Football Union's appeal council yesterday.
"I'm stunned and flabbergasted by the decision not to overturn the appeal," McCallion said today.
"I'm bloody disappointed because in the first place we didn't think the suspension was warranted and it makes it even harder for us this week against North Harbour."

Lidgard was handed the penalty after being found guilty of excessive rucking on Otago halfback Mark Chapman-Smith during their National Provincial Championship (NPC) first division match a fortnight ago.
Nevertheless, McCallion was impressed with Matt Filipo, who filled in for Lidgard against Taranaki last weekend, a match Counties lost 34-16.
"I think our forwards went well on the day, our backs lost direction once Danny Love (first five-eighth) went off injured and that is where we let ourselves down," he said.
"But we did something other teams have so far failed to do against Taranaki and that is to have our forwards take lineout pill against them. I was pleased with that aspect of our game."
He said next Sunday's game against North Harbour was a grand opportunity to put the Knights out of their misery for good this season.
"They're probably a bit stunned with the shield challenge last Friday, they have to regroup and they're probably feeling a bit sorry for themselves," he said.
"It's a big opportunity for us to capitalise on that but first we have to get our house back in order for the game."
North Harbour needed to win four games straight to have a show of making the playoffs.
"We can afford to drop one, but like heck we want to do that to oblige them. It is a crucial game, still more so for them than us."
McCallion will name his team tomorrow night after their first training session this week.
